title: What to do when a debt collector contacts you about a collection account
meta_description: A simple guide to debt collection notices, written disputes, credit reports, and your rights when a collector contacts you.
summary: A call or letter about a collection account can feel urgent. You do not have to decide on the spot whether the amount is right. Start by writing down who contacted you, what they said, and when. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) recommends keeping letters, copies, and notes of conversations.

title: What is a debt validation letter, and what should it ask for?
meta_description: Learn what a debt validation letter does, what to include, and what happens after a timely written dispute under federal law.
summary: A debt validation letter is your written reply when a covered debt collector says you owe a debt and you need to check it. It can dispute all or part of the claim, request the original creditor's name and address, or both. The law gives special protection to a written dispute or request made during the validation period. 15 U.S.C. § 1692g · CFPB rule

title: What does a Form 1099-C mean for your credit and your taxes?
meta_description: Understand what Form 1099-C reports, why it does not settle every debt or credit-report question, and when to ask a tax professional.
summary: A Form 1099-C can arrive when a creditor reports cancellation of debt. It is a tax-reporting form, not a complete answer to whether you still owe money or whether a credit-report entry is right. The IRS even says that if a creditor keeps trying to collect after sending the form, the debt may not have been canceled. Verify your situation with the creditor. IRS Topic 431

title: How to make your first credit report dispute: simple, specific and documented
meta_description: A plain-English guide to finding a credit-report error, writing a focused first dispute, keeping records, and checking the response.
summary: Your first credit-report dispute does not need a legal argument. Say what the report shows, why it is wrong, and what records support you. This is separate from a debt-validation request to a collector. CFPB dispute guide

title: If your debt was sold: what to look for in the paperwork
meta_description: Learn how to read a debt sale's bill of sale, account schedule, ownership chain and warranty language without assuming missing pages decide your case.
summary: A creditor can sell a consumer debt to a buyer; that buyer may later sell it again. A sale does not make a debt unreal or require a new agreement with each buyer. When someone collects or sues, ask who is claiming the right to collect this particular account, and what connects the account to that claimant? The CFPB explains that debts can be sold. Whether a collector or plaintiff must show a particular document depends on the setting and applicable law.
